subsystems.name: Root uptake system
subsystems.role: pulls metal ions out of soil water and into root cells.
parts: metal transporter proteins (ZIP and NRAMP families)
proton pumps that acidify the rhizosphere

subsystems.name: Long-distance transport
subsystems.role: moves the metal from root to shoot in the xylem.

subsystems.name: Leaf storage
subsystems.role: packages the metal safely so the plant survives its own harvest.

subsystems.name: Agronomic system
subsystems.role: grows the crop on contaminated land like any other field crop.

subsystems.name: Biomass processing
subsystems.role: turns metal-rich plant matter into a concentrated product.

buildSteps.title: Pick the metal and the host
buildSteps.detail: Choose what to extract — nickel, cadmium, zinc or arsenic — then decide between a natural hyperaccumulator with modest yields and a high-biomass crop that must be engineered to take up far more.

buildSteps.title: Find the genes
buildSteps.detail: Search hyperaccumulator species for the transporters and chelator enzymes that make them exceptional, and test each candidate in ordinary fast-growing plants in the lab.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the plant
buildSteps.detail: Insert extra copies of metal transporter genes, or boost chelator production, using Agrobacterium-mediated transformation; where the species allows, use CRISPR to lift the brakes on uptake. Many hyperaccumulators are hard to transform, so this step is often the bottleneck.

buildSteps.title: Screen for tolerance and load
buildSteps.detail: Grow candidate lines in metal-spiked soil and on real contaminated ground, selecting lines that accumulate the most metal without stunted growth — the two traits trade off against each other.

buildSteps.title: Run confined field trials
buildSteps.detail: Plant small plots on contaminated land and measure a full mass balance: how many tonnes of dry biomass per hectare, and how many milligrams of metal per kilogram of that biomass.

buildSteps.title: Grow the crop
buildSteps.detail: Manage the field as a normal crop — pH, water, weeds, pests — while monitoring that irrigation does not wash metal deeper or off-site.

buildSteps.title: Harvest and remove
buildSteps.detail: Cut and remove the whole above-ground biomass; removal is what actually decontaminates the soil, so nothing may be ploughed back in.

buildSteps.title: Concentrate the biomass
buildSteps.detail: Dry and burn or gasify the harvest to cut its volume by an order of magnitude, leaving an ash that is rich enough in metal to be called a bio-ore.

buildSteps.title: Recover the metal
buildSteps.detail: Smelt or leach the ash, then electrowin or precipitate a saleable metal salt — for nickel, typically a sulphate or carbonate — and repeat the planting cycle for years until soil concentrations fall.

prerequisites.why: routine in a few model and crop species, but most natural hyperaccumulators are still hard to engineer.
decades of work on transporter and chelator genes has mapped the pathways that control uptake.

prerequisites.tech: Long-term field trials on contaminated land
prerequisites.why: multi-year plots are needed because removal per harvest is slow and soil is heterogeneous.
without affordable ashing and refining, the metal-rich harvest is just expensive waste.

pathway.milestone: field phytoremediation using natural hyperaccumulators — for example nickel accumulating shrubs on ultramafic soils, and arsenic-hyperaccumulating ferns on contaminated sites
pathway.unlocks: a working but slow and niche cleanup method, and in a few places small-scale metal recovery that partly pays for itself.

pathway.milestone: engineered high-biomass crops carrying boosted transporter genes, tested in multi-year field trials
pathway.unlocks: faster metal removal per hectare than wild species can deliver.

pathway.milestone: integrated phytomining, where harvested bio-ore is refined and sold
pathway.unlocks: contaminated and naturally metal-rich land treated as a low-grade ore body rather than a liability.

pathway.milestone: routine phytoextraction of cadmium and zinc from farmland
pathway.unlocks: lower dietary exposure to toxic metals in staple crops.
